name: Spell Stone
body:
Price Varies Aura Varies; CL V.; Weight 1/2 lb.

DESCRIPTION

A spell stone is a small piece of slate etched with a series of runes. If snapped in half, the spell stone releases the spell stores within as if the user has cast it. Spell stones are only usable once. A spell stone is created with a spell etched on it up to a maximum spell level of 4th level, with a casting time of less than 1 minute. A user of a spell stone need not be able to cast the spell normally or Use Magic Device to activate the spell stone.

The price of spell stones is equal to the level of the spell x the caster level of the spell stored within x 100 gp. If the spell etched into the spell stone has a material cost, it is added to the base price and cost to create. Note that some spells appear at different levels for different casters. The level of such spells depends on the caster creating the spell stone. The creator or user of a spell stone cannot apply metamagic or any feats that would normally affect the spell, like Spell Focus or Augment

You can apply one metamagic feat you know to the wand to which the metamagic wand grip is attached.

Doing so drains one additional charge per spell level increase normally required by the metamagic feat. The level increase for this purpose is not reduced by any class abilities or feats. For example, you couple apply Extend Spell to a spell cast from a wand by expending two charges because Extend Spell normally increases the spell level by one.

CONSTRUCTION REQUIREMENTS

Cost 3,000 gp; Feats Craft Wondrous Item, Metamagic Spell Trigger

Identifying Spell Stones: A spell stone can be identified in a similar manner to a scroll.

Activating a Spell Stone: As mentioned before, a spell stone is activated by snapping the slate in half.

The user of the spell stone is treated as the caster and may choose the target of the spell stored within as if they were the caster. However, the spell stone uses the caster level of the creator and the spellcasting attribute of the spell for the spell effects and DC is equal to the minimum required to cast a spell of that spell’s level.

For example, a 1st level spell would require a minimum of an 11 in the requisite ability score, so the ability score bonus would be +0.

Activating the spell stone is a standard action that provokes an attack of opportunity. Unlike spellcasting, or using spell completion items, the spell from the stone cannot be lost and does not require a concentration check. A spell stone broken or destroyed by other means does not release the spell.
